eyebrow: Online marketing course · taught in Azerbaijani
lede: A 3-month online programme that covers marketing end to end: understanding the market and the customer, building a brand, setting prices, planning campaigns and measuring results. Taught by Hasanali Ildirimov.
summary: The Marketing Course is Marketing School's 3-month online marketing programme, taught in Azerbaijani. Across 9 modules it covers customer and market research, competitor analysis, brand positioning, pricing, campaign planning, channels and measurement. Lessons are recorded and can be watched at any time; live Q&A sessions run on the 2nd and 4th Saturday of every month, homework is based on real business cases, and every student gets a one-to-one mentoring session after completing the lessons. The course costs 99 AZN per month. Students who meet the assessment threshold receive a diploma. The instructor is Hasanali Ildirimov, Head of the Non-Food Category at Azersun Holding.
focus: Marketing decisions: market, customer, brand, price, campaigns
card_text: Research the market and your customers, position a brand, set prices, plan campaigns and measure the results — all on real cases.
overview: The course brings together every core part of marketing: researching the market and the customer, positioning a brand, setting prices, planning campaigns, choosing channels and measuring results. Each module combines video lessons with homework based on a real business case. Twice a month, on the 2nd and 4th Saturday, the instructor answers your questions live, and once you have completed the lessons you book a one-to-one mentoring session.

features.title: Real cases
features.text: Homework is built on real company cases, not textbook examples, so you learn to make decisions with incomplete information.

features.title: Evidence-based methods
features.text: The programme is built on well-researched marketing principles with proven results, not on fashionable tactics that don't work.

features.title: Speaking in numbers
features.text: Every module ends with measurement: which metric changes, what to compare it with and what decision to make.

modules.title: Marketing fundamentals
modules.text: What marketing is for, which decisions it covers and which common beliefs are wrong.

modules.title: Customer and market research
modules.text: Designing surveys, running interviews and reading the results to understand your customers properly.

modules.title: Competitor analysis
modules.text: What market share is, how to track competitors and which indicators to watch.

modules.title: Brand positioning
modules.text: Expressing a brand's place in one sentence. Colour, logo and slogan — the assets that make a brand recognisable.

modules.title: Growing a brand
modules.text: Winning new customers, expanding distribution and keeping the brand front of mind.

modules.title: Pricing
modules.text: How prices are set and how discounts affect sales and the brand.

modules.title: Campaign planning
modules.text: Writing a brief, choosing channels, allocating the budget and evaluating advertising.

modules.title: Channels and execution
modules.text: TV, digital and retail — planning and executing channels together.

modules.title: Measurement and reporting
modules.text: Which metrics to track, how to build a report and how to present it to management.
